How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  February 5, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Michael Muse, Recreation Supervisor
  Danielle Adriano, Recreation Coordinator

SUBJECT:  Holiday Tree Lighting Event Recap

On Tuesday, December 5 the community enjoyed an enhanced Holiday Tree Lighting
event at Plaza Park. The festivities started at 6pm with entertainment provided by Dewey
Wood Craft Rangers, the Polynesian/Hawaiian dance class from the Community Services
Department, Gabrielino Choir and San Gabriel High School marching band. At 7pm, after
welcoming remarks, the Mayor and City Council led a countdown to light the tree and
welcomed Santa Claus to the event, escorted by the San Gabriel Police and Fire
Department.

In addition to the traditional Santa photo booth and ornament making opportunity, this
event provided enhanced elements such as surprise snow fall as the tree was lit. Also
added this year was a trackless train and a Taste of San Gabriel. The Taste of San Gabriel
sought to show case the amazing local food found in San Gabriel.

In this inaugural year we had participation from D’ange Bakery, Jasmine Creamery, El Pavo
Bakery, Paris Baguette, Bay Poke, and Dancing Spoons. It is estimated that there were
over 2,000 community members that enjoyed the evening.

While the refreshed experience was well received it provided an opportunity for the
department to make improvements for next year. In particular increased supplies and
staffing to accommodate the high demand at the ornament making booth. Staff will also
develop a queuing process for pictures with Santa and the trackless train, perhaps pre-
registration similar to the haunted zone at Fall Fun Festival. Given the success of this
year’s event the department has already begun looking for creative ways to maintain the
success with budget conscious solutions.
   City of San Gabriel
  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  February 5, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Danielle Adriano, Recreation Coordinator

SUBJECT:  Turkey Trot Event Recap

The 46th Annual Turkey Trot was scheduled to take place on Saturday, November 18 at
Vincent Lugo Park. However, due to inclement weather and out of an abundance of
caution, the event was postponed until Sunday, November 19. Despite the sudden
change, the event successfully had a total of over 320 spectators with 152 registered
participants.

Early bird registration began on September 1 and registrants were guaranteed a
commemorative finisher medal, t-shirt, refreshments, and a photocopy of the traditional
route. New this year, was a turn-by-turn navigation for the 5K/10K route for runners who
downloaded the free “RunGo” app. In addition, a DJ and coffee food truck were added to
the event.

The 30 volunteers from the Gabrielino High School Interact Club and Key Club provided
crucial assistance to the event by giving direction and refreshments to runners as they
passed by. Custom winner medals were handed out to the top three runners in each age
division as well as over 40 raffle prizes to those in attendance. Staff continue to look for
creative ways to enhance this growing community event including smoother day of
registration and packet distribution.

Staff extend gratitude to Councilmember Chan and Vice Chair Duong for their assistance
with medal distribution throughout the event.

The title sponsor was Athens Services, and the gold sponsor was San Gabriel Nursery and
Florist. Athens Services and the San Gabriel Police Department hosted booths and
provided give-a-ways for event participants.

The San Gabriel Fire, Police, and Public Works Departments provided logistical support
which was essential to the success of the event.
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  February 5, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  Draft 2024 Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2024 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting. The draft for 2024 outlined in this report
includes items from the 2023 workplan and the amendments made at the November 6,
2023 commission meeting.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 DRAFT ANNUAL WORKPLAN 2024
The 2024 Workplan sets forth four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Collaborate with businesses/organizations in order to offer additional social
  services to older adult
  i. For example: Collaborating with businesses offering tracking
  devices/systems for older adults with memory related health issues
  b. Provide programs for residents aged 18-64 with an emphasis on teen
  programs
  c. Continue offering and expand the internship program for youth to assist
  with translation services
  d. Serve as a liaison for events that City Council has requested be expanded or
  added. Commission members to provide feedback and support for these
  events

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Continue to support health services by partnering with health service
  providers
  i. Examples include: Herald Christian Health Center and USC School of
  Pharmacy
  b. Develop and implement a Community Services Department Day advertising
  all programs, events and services offered by the Community Services
  Department
  c. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.

  3. Embrace and Celebrate Community Diversity
  a. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to
  assist in the development and implementation of events and services
  i. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native
  American Community and interfaith groups
 4. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
  b. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  i. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
  c. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  i. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information
  d. Recommend that City Council approve the release of an RFP for a new
  registration software during fiscal year 2024/25.
